problem.title: Continuity of the quantum channel capacity

question.summary: The source asked whether the unassisted quantum (coherent) capacity is a continuous function of the channel in cb-norm. Leung and Smith proved uniform continuity for channels with fixed finite output dimension, including at zero-capacity channels.
question.importance: Continuity means that a noise model known only up to a small cb-norm uncertainty still determines the available transmission rate up to a vanishing error, which matters for capacity analysis and fault-tolerant design; only lower semi-continuity was known, and the regularisation over unboundedly many channel uses made upper semi-continuity delicate.

targetClauses.label: Continuity of the quantum capacity
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks whether the unassisted quantum (coherent) capacity Q is a continuous function on the convex set of channels between fixed finite-dimensional input and output spaces, equipped with the cb-norm distance.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A proof of continuity, or a pair or sequence of channels along which Q jumps discontinuously.

claims.title: Leung and Smith prove uniform continuity of quantum capacity
claims.text: Leung and Smith prove uniform continuity of the ordinary unassisted quantum capacity for channels with fixed finite output dimension, bounding the change in Q for two channels at diamond distance at most epsilon by an explicit function of epsilon and the output dimension that tends to zero with epsilon. Their entropy-telescoping proof applies on the entire channel set, including channels of zero capacity, so the archived question is answered affirmatively.

evidence.sourceLocator: Continuity theorem for the unassisted quantum capacity
evidence.label: Communications in Mathematical Physics

decisions.rationale: The cited peer-reviewed theorem establishes uniform continuity of the unassisted quantum capacity on the whole channel set, which is exactly what the archived statement asks.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: The interior-of-positive-capacity qualification in the same paper concerns quantum capacities assisted by free backward or two-way public classical communication; it does not qualify the theorem for the unassisted capacity Q asked about here.
